**Axis 1 Convolution:** Apply 1D Gaussian convolution along the first axis (e.g., x-axis) to produce an intermediate volume $V_{xy}$.
**Axis 2 Convolution:** Apply 1D Gaussian convolution along the second axis (e.g., y-axis) to $V_{xy}$ to produce $V_{xyz}$.
**Axis 3 Convolution:** Apply 1D Gaussian convolution along the third axis (e.g., z-axis) to $V_{xyz}$ to produce the final blurred volume $V_{blur}$.
- Boundary conditions must be handled during convolution (e.g., padding or clamping) to avoid artifacts at the volume edges.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot R)$, where $N$ is the number of voxels and $R$ is the filter radius.
The separability reduces the complexity from $O(N \cdot R^3)$ for a direct 3D convolution to $O(N \cdot R)$.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for storing the volume and intermediate results.
- **When to use:** When interactive performance is critical and edge preservation is not the primary concern.
- **When not to use:** When edge preservation is required; consider the [Bilateral Filter](8983-bilateral-filter.md) instead.
